passages.text: Woe is me! For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave.
passages.sermon:
Micah is a prophet of God.
\r\nMicah speaks with sorrow.
\r\nMicah says, "Woe is me!"
\r\nMicah feels deep sadness.
\r\nMicah feels like a person gathering fruit at the end of summer.
\r\nMicah feels like someone gleaning in a vineyard after the harvest.
\r\nMicah finds nothing left to gather.
\r\nMicah sees no cluster of grapes to eat.
\r\nMicah cannot find an early fig.
\r\nMicah desires the first ripe fruit, but it is not there.
passages.original: אַ֣לְלַי לִ֗י כִּ֤י הָיִ֙יתִי֙ כְּאָסְפֵּי־ קַ֔יִץ כְּעֹלְלֹ֖ת בָּצִ֑יר אֵין־ אֶשְׁכּ֣וֹל לֶאֱכ֔וֹל בִּכּוּרָ֖ה אִוְּתָ֥ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: The godly man has perished from the earth; there is no one upright among men. They all lie in wait for blood; they hunt one another with a net.
passages.sermon:
There are no godly people left on the earth.
No one among men is upright.
All people wait to shed blood.
Each person hunts his brother with a net.
passages.original: אָבַ֤ד חָסִיד֙ מִן־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְיָשָׁ֥ר בָּאָדָ֖ם אָ֑יִן כֻּלָּם֙ לְדָמִ֣ים יֶאֱרֹ֔בוּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ אָחִ֖יהוּ יָצ֥וּדוּ חֵֽרֶם׃

passages.text: Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.
passages.sermon:
The people use both hands to do evil.
The prince asks for a bribe.
The judge also wants payment.
The powerful man speaks out his evil desire.
All of them join together to do wrong.
passages.original: עַל־ הָרַ֤ע כַּפַּ֙יִם֙ לְהֵיטִ֔יב הַשַּׂ֣ר שֹׁאֵ֔ל וְהַשֹּׁפֵ֖ט בַּשִׁלּ֑וּם וְהַגָּד֗וֹל דֹּבֵ֨ר הַוַּ֥ת נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ה֖וּא וַֽיְעַבְּתֽוּהָ׃

passages.text: The best of them is like a brier; the most upright is sharper than a hedge of thorns. The day for your watchmen has come, the day of your visitation. Now is the time of their confusion.
passages.sermon:
The people in this passage are corrupt and violent.
The best person among them is like a brier.
A brier is sharp and harmful.
The most upright person among them is sharper than a hedge of thorns.
A hedge of thorns is painful and dangerous.
The day for your watchmen has come.
This is the day of your visitation.
Now is the time of their confusion.
passages.original: טוֹבָ֣ם כְּחֵ֔דֶק יָשָׁ֖ר מִמְּסוּכָ֑ה י֤וֹם מְצַפֶּ֙יךָ֙ פְּקֻדָּתְךָ֣ בָ֔אָה עַתָּ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה מְבוּכָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Do not rely on a friend; do not trust in a companion. Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.
passages.sermon: Do not trust a friend.\r\nDo not put confidence in a close companion.\r\nGuard your words from the woman who lies in your arms.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ בְרֵ֔עַ אַֽל־ תִּבְטְח֖וּ בְּאַלּ֑וּף מִשֹּׁכֶ֣בֶת חֵיקֶ֔ךָ שְׁמֹ֖ר פִּתְחֵי־ פִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man’s enemies are the members of his own household.
passages.sermon:
A son brings shame to his father.
A daughter stands against her mother.
A daughter-in-law opposes her mother-in-law.
A man finds his enemies in his own household.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ בֵן֙ מְנַבֵּ֣ל אָ֔ב בַּ֚ת קָמָ֣ה בְאִמָּ֔הּ כַּלָּ֖ה בַּחֲמֹתָ֑הּ אֹיְבֵ֥י אִ֖ישׁ אַנְשֵׁ֥י בֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
passages.sermon:
I am a believer in the LORD.
I will look to the LORD.
I will wait for the God who saves me.
My God will hear me.
passages.original: וַאֲנִי֙ בַּיהוָ֣ה אֲצַפֶּ֔ה אוֹחִ֖ילָה לֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעִ֑י יִשְׁמָעֵ֖נִי אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
passages.sermon:
My enemy, do not gloat over me.
I have fallen.
But I will rise.
I sit in darkness.
But the LORD is my light.
passages.original: אַֽל־ תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י אֹיַ֙בְתִּי֙ לִ֔י כִּ֥י נָפַ֖לְתִּי קָ֑מְתִּי כִּֽי־ אֵשֵׁ֣ב בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ יְהוָ֖ה א֥וֹר לִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.
passages.sermon:
I have sinned against the LORD.
I must endure the LORD’s anger.
I will endure His anger until He argues my case.
He will execute justice for me.
He will bring me into the light.
I will see His righteousness.
passages.original: זַ֤עַף יְהוָה֙ אֶשָּׂ֔א כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אתִי ל֑וֹ עַד֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֤יב רִיבִי֙ וְעָשָׂ֣ה מִשְׁפָּטִ֔י יוֹצִיאֵ֣נִי לָא֔וֹר אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּצִדְקָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame— she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
passages.sermon:
My enemy will see what happens.
My enemy will feel shame.
This enemy once said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?”
I will see my enemy with my own eyes.
At that time, people will trample my enemy like mud in the streets.
passages.original: וְתֵרֶ֤א אֹיַ֙בְתִּי֙ וּתְכַסֶּ֣הָ בוּשָׁ֔ה הָאֹמְרָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י אַיּ֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יִךְ עֵינַי֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ינָּה בָּ֔הּ עַתָּ֛ה תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לְמִרְמָ֖ס כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The day for rebuilding your walls will come— the day for extending your boundary.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He promises a day will come.
On that day, you will rebuild your walls.
On that day, your boundary will be extended.
passages.original: י֖וֹם לִבְנ֣וֹת גְּדֵרָ֑יִךְ י֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יִרְחַק־ חֹֽק׃

passages.text: On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, even from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
passages.sermon:
On that day, people will come to you.
They will come from Assyria.
They will come from the cities of Egypt.
They will come from Egypt to the Euphrates River.
They will come from sea to sea.
They will come from mountain to mountain.
passages.original: י֥וֹם הוּא֙ וְעָדֶ֣יךָ יָב֔וֹא לְמִנִּ֥י אַשּׁ֖וּר וְעָרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר וּלְמִנִּ֤י מָצוֹר֙ וְעַד־ נָהָ֔ר וְיָ֥ם מִיָּ֖ם וְהַ֥ר הָהָֽר׃

passages.text: Then the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds.
passages.sermon:
God will judge the people for their actions.
The earth will become empty and ruined.
The people who live there have done evil things.
Their deeds will cause this destruction.
The land will suffer because of what its people have done.
passages.original: וְהָיְתָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ לִשְׁמָמָ֖ה עַל־ יֹֽשְׁבֶ֑יהָ מִפְּרִ֖י מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Shepherd with Your staff Your people, the flock of Your inheritance. They live alone in a woodland, surrounded by pastures. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
passages.sermon:
God, shepherd Your people with Your staff.
Your people are the flock of Your inheritance.
They live alone.
They dwell in a woodland among pastures.
Let them graze in Bashan.
Let them graze in Gilead.
Let them live as they did in ancient days.
passages.original: רְעֵ֧ה עַמְּךָ֣ בְשִׁבְטֶ֗ךָ צֹ֚אן נַֽחֲלָתֶ֔ךָ שֹׁכְנִ֣י לְבָדָ֔ד יַ֖עַר בְּת֣וֹךְ כַּרְמֶ֑ל יִרְע֥וּ בָשָׁ֛ן וְגִלְעָ֖ד כִּימֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God reminds them of the time they left Egypt.
God did great wonders for them then.
God promises to show wonders again.
God will act as He did in the days of the Exodus.
passages.original: כִּימֵ֥י צֵאתְךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אַרְאֶ֖נּוּ נִפְלָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Nations will see and be ashamed, deprived of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
passages.sermon:
Nations will see God's actions.
They will feel ashamed.
They will lose all their strength.
They will cover their mouths with their hands.
Their ears will stop hearing.
passages.original: יִרְא֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ וְיֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מִכֹּ֖ל גְּבֽוּרָתָ֑ם יָשִׂ֤ימוּ יָד֙ עַל־ פֶּ֔ה אָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם תֶּחֱרַֽשְׁנָה׃

passages.text: They will lick the dust like a snake, like reptiles slithering on the ground. They will crawl from their holes in the presence of the LORD our God; they will tremble in fear of You.
passages.sermon:
The nations will act in fear before the LORD our God.
They will lick the dust like a snake.
They will slither on the ground like crawling creatures.
They will come out of their hiding places.
They will tremble before the LORD our God.
They will be afraid of You.
passages.original: יְלַחֲכ֤וּ עָפָר֙ כַּנָּחָ֔שׁ כְּזֹחֲלֵ֣י אֶ֔רֶץ יִרְגְּז֖וּ מִמִּסְגְּרֹֽתֵיהֶ֑ם אֶל־ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ יִפְחָ֔דוּ וְיִֽרְא֖וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance— who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?
passages.sermon:
God is unique.
No other god is like Him.
God forgives iniquity.
God passes over the transgression of His people.
His people are the remnant of His inheritance.
God does not stay angry forever.
God delights in showing loving devotion.
passages.original: מִי־ אֵ֣ל כָּמ֗וֹךָ נֹשֵׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְעֹבֵ֣ר עַל־ פֶּ֔שַׁע לִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית נַחֲלָת֑וֹ לֹא־ הֶחֱזִ֤יק לָעַד֙ אַפּ֔וֹ כִּֽי־ חָפֵ֥ץ חֶ֖סֶד הֽוּא׃

passages.text: He will again have compassion on us; He will vanquish our iniquities. You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea.
passages.sermon:
God is merciful.
God will show compassion to us again.
God will defeat our iniquities.
God will remove all our sins.
God will throw all our sins into the depths of the sea.
passages.original: יָשׁ֣וּב יְרַֽחֲמֵ֔נוּ יִכְבֹּ֖שׁ עֲוֺֽנֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְתַשְׁלִ֛יךְ בִּמְצֻל֥וֹת יָ֖ם כָּל־ חַטֹּאותָֽם׃

passages.text: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
passages.sermon:
God is faithful.
God keeps His promises.
God promised Jacob.
God promised Abraham.
God shows faithfulness to Jacob.
God shows loving devotion to Abraham.
God swore these promises to our fathers long ago.
God fulfills what He swore from ancient times.
passages.original: תִּתֵּ֤ן אֱמֶת֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב חֶ֖סֶד לְאַבְרָהָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר־ נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ מִ֥ימֵי קֶֽדֶם׃
